samples.summary: The durable client outlives the election it depends on: the decision is latched in `held.current` but `useDurableDocument` releases the Web Lock when the preference flips off
samples.evidence: `held.current` is written once per `subject` (line 242-244) and deliberately never re-read from `durable`, so the `DurableYorkieProvider` with `clientKey = wb:{userId}:{docKey}` and the store stays mounted for the life of the open document. But `useDurableDocument`'s effect (use-durable-document.ts:152-181) has `eligible` in its dependency list, so when `useOfflinePersistenceEnabled()` flips to false the cleanup runs and calls `handle.release()` — freeing `wb-durable:{userId}:{docKey}` while this tab is still writing under the stable client key. Both halves are pinned by tests: use-durable-document.test.tsx 'gives the election back when it is switched off' asserts `locks.held.size === 0`, and collab-document-provider-durable.test.tsx 'keeps its client when the preference changes underneath it' asserts the durable clientKey is still mounted. If the preference is then turned back on and the same document is opened in a second tab, that tab wins the now-free election and mounts a client with the *identical* stable key — the shared-actor / colliding-clientSeq case the whole election exists to prevent (durable-session.ts:11-24), i.e. silent edit loss. Even without a second tab, the tab keeps writing document content to disk after the user switched local saving off.

samples.summary: `dropAllForUser` records the `evicted` marker on the erasing store instance, which is never the instance the durable client writes through — so post-erase appends are silently ignored while the chip still reports `saved-locally`
samples.evidence: `dropAllForUser` purges each key and then does `this.evicted.add(docKey)` (line 858-862) so that a later `appendChange` throws instead of being silently ignored (`refuseIfEvicted`, line 617-626, reading `this.evicted`, a per-instance `Set` declared line ~/`private readonly evicted`). But `evicted` is per-instance and the erase never runs on the instance the SDK holds: `watchForOfflineDisable` is handed `() => store` from OfflineRuntime's own `new WafflebaseDocStore(...)` (offline-runtime.tsx:55-70), and `eraseOfflineDataOnLogout` constructs a throwaway `new WafflebaseDocStore({userId: who})` (offline-erase.ts:123), while the live client writes through the store created in `DurableYorkieProvider` (durable-yorkie-provider.tsx:86-97). That instance's `evicted` set stays empty, so its `appendChange` takes the `!header` branch (wafflebase-doc-store.ts:540-541, 560-563) and resolves successfully with nothing written, while `useDocumentDurability()` still answers true and the chip keeps showing 'Saved to this device'. Worse on the logout path: the next `saveSnapshot` from the still-mounted client re-creates the just-erased entry, putting the signed-out user's document content back on disk after the erase logout promised.

samples.summary: `documentIdsIn` filters on `document.workspaceId` using what the call site passes as the workspace *slug*, so the workspace-delete purge silently matches nothing
samples.evidence: `deleteWorkspace(id)` is called as `deleteWorkspace(workspaceId!)` from the `/w/:workspaceId/settings` route param (workspace-settings.tsx:182), and that param is a slug — the same file navigates with `/w/${updated.slug}/settings` (line 103) and `/w/${remaining[0].slug}` (line 189). `documentIdsIn` then compares that slug to `document.workspaceId` (workspaces.ts:98), which is the document's workspace **id** (types/documents.ts:41, populated from the backend's `workspaceId` column). The filter therefore yields `[]` for every real deletion, `purgeOfflineDocuments([])` returns immediately (offline-erase.ts:148), and the local copies of a deleted workspace's documents stay on disk until the thirty-day sweep — exactly the outcome this code was added to prevent. The same mismatch applies to `removeMember`'s `documentIdsIn(workspaceId)` (line 138). Nothing fails loudly, so the no-op is invisible.

samples.summary: Nothing lowers `durable` when the store fails or refuses its writes, so the chip can promise `saved-locally` for work that is not on disk
samples.evidence: `SyncSignals.durable` is documented as the conjunction of three facts, one of which is 'the store is not failing its writes' (sync-status/sync-state.ts:40-48). The only thing that ever lowers it is `reportLoss`, latched solely from the SDK's `local-changes-dropped` event (durable-yorkie-provider.tsx:104-105, 160-163). A store write that rejects — `withQuotaRetry` giving up after one eviction (wafflebase-doc-store.ts:1081-1084), `refuseIfEvicted` throwing, or `open()` rejecting because IndexedDB is unavailable — never reaches `reportLoss`, and neither does the silent `!header` no-op path. `useDocumentDurability()` therefore keeps answering true and `deriveSyncState` keeps returning `saved-locally`, i.e. the chip tells the user their unsent work survives a reload when it is not on disk. This is the one direction the design says the feature must not fail in.
searchedFor: read wafflebase-doc-store.ts error paths (withQuotaRetry, refuseIfEvicted, appendChange, saveMeta)

samples.summary: `DurableYorkieProvider` never closes the `WafflebaseDocStore` it creates, leaking one IndexedDB connection per document opened, and creates one store per document despite the doc comment claiming one per client key
samples.evidence: The store is built in `useMemo(..., [userId])` (lines 86-97) and there is no `useEffect` cleanup calling `store.close()`, so every document opened in a session leaves an open `IDBDatabase` connection alive for the life of the tab. The comment above it (lines 69-75) states the store is 'created once per client key' and warns that 're-creating it per document would give each one its own `touched` set' — but this component *is* mounted per document, so exactly that happens; only the `isOpenElsewhere: isOpenInAnyTab` callback compensates, and only for documents that hold an election. The leaked connections also mean a future `deleteDatabase`-based erase would be blocked (the versionchange handler closes, but the rows-based erase path opens yet more connections).

samples.summary: The fallback store created inside `watchForOfflineDisable` is never closed
samples.evidence: `const current = store() ?? new WafflebaseDocStore({ userId: who });` (line 205) — when the app has no store to lend, a fresh one is constructed, used by the fire-and-forget `eraseOfflineData(...)` (line 213) and then dropped with no `close()`, unlike `eraseOfflineDataOnLogout` and `purgeOfflineDocuments` which both close in a `finally`. Each toggle-off in an environment without an open store leaks an IndexedDB connection.

samples.summary: `eraseOfflineDataOnLogout` forgets the identity before the erase has succeeded, so a failed erase can never be retried
samples.evidence: `rememberOfflineUser(undefined)` runs at line 119, before `eraseOfflineData(store, who)` at line 125. If the erase throws (the catch at 126 swallows it), both the module state and the `wafflebase-offline-user` localStorage mirror have already been cleared, so `offlineUserId()` answers undefined for every later path — no subsequent logout, purge or disable-watch can attribute the leftover rows, and the signed-out user's document content sits on the device until the thirty-day sweep. Clearing after a successful erase would preserve the retry.

samples.summary: A release followed immediately by a re-acquire in the same tab can be refused, silently downgrading the reopened document to non-durable
samples.evidence: `release()` deletes the election entry and calls `releaseLock()` synchronously (lines 179-185), but the real Web Lock is only freed when the parked callback promise *settles* — a turn of the loop later (the adapter at lines ~/`webLocks()` resolves `releaseHeld`, and the test file itself notes a `flush()` is needed before the name is free, durable-session.test.ts 'holds the name for as long as the session lives'). A document unmount/remount in the same tab (React StrictMode, navigating away and straight back, or `subject` changing) re-requests with `ifAvailable: true`, gets `null`, and resolves `undefined`. Nothing retries, because `useDurableDocument`'s effect dependencies did not change afterwards, so the reopened document stays non-durable for the rest of that open.

samples.summary: When `snapshotWatermark` cannot answer, `rehydrateArchive` performs no contiguity check at all yet still reports `complete: true` for a log with holes
samples.evidence: `expected` is left `undefined` when `watermark === undefined` (lines 187-188), which disables the gap test at line 196, and `complete` is computed purely from `truncatedAt === undefined` (line 238). A log missing an entry is then replayed across the hole and handed back labelled complete — precisely the 'plausible-looking document missing an edit, handed back with no sign that anything is absent' the surrounding comment argues must not happen. Reachable whenever `getPendingChangesAfter`/`getCheckpoint` are unavailable or throw (snapshotWatermark's own catch returns undefined). `complete: false` would be the honest fallback when contiguity cannot be checked.

samples.summary: OfflineRuntime opens the offline database and runs the sweep/archive listing on every login even when the feature cannot possibly have written anything
samples.evidence: The effect at lines 50-97 unconditionally constructs a `WafflebaseDocStore`, runs `collectStale()` and `listRecoverableWork()`, with no check on `supportsClientKey()` or `getOfflinePersistenceEnabled()`. On this branch `supportsClientKey()` is false (package.json pins `@yorkie-js/react` 0.7.22 while `MinClientKeyVersion` is 0.7.23), so the store can never have content, yet every signed-in user gets a `wafflebase-offline` IndexedDB database created and swept on each mount. Harmless in outcome, but it makes a never-written database appear on every user's device and pays an IDB open on each `userId` change.

finding.summary: The durable client outlives the election it depends on: the decision is latched in `held.current` but `useDurableDocument` releases the Web Lock when the preference flips off

Both halves are pinned by tests: use-durable-document.test.tsx 'gives the election back when it is switched off' asserts `locks.held.size === 0`, and collab-document-provider-durable.test.tsx 'keeps its client when the preference changes underneath it' asserts the durable clientKey is still mounted. If the preference is then turned back on and the same document is opened in a second tab, that tab wins the now-free election and mounts a client with the *identical* stable key — the shared-actor / colliding-clientSeq case the whole election exists to prevent (durable-session.ts:11-24), i.e. silent edit loss. verdict.reason: Both halves are present exactly as described. collab-document-provider.tsx:229 builds `subject` from user id and docKey only, and 242-244 latches `{subject, durable, clientKey}` once; 245-248 and 277-300 render DurableYorkieProvider from that latched value, with no path that re-decides on a preference change (only `giveUp`/`stoodDown` at 236-239/296 can demote). Meanwhile use-durable-document.ts:126-131 folds the live preference into `eligible`, and the effect at 152-181 has `eligible` in its dep list with a cleanup (177-180) that calls `handle?.release()`, which frees the Web Lock via durable-session.ts:175-187. `useOfflinePersistenceEnabled` is reactive (offline-persistence-preference.ts:102-121), so flipping the toggle in Settings or another tab fires this. Result: the tab keeps a client mounted under the stable key `wb:{userId}:{docKey}` with the IndexedDB store attached (durable-yorkie-provider.tsx:86-124) while the election that makes that key safe has been given back — the exact precondition durable-session.ts:9-23 says must hold to avoid a shared actor and colliding clientSeq. Both behaviors are pinned by tests (collab-document-provider-durable.test.tsx:294-314; use-durable-document.test.tsx:172-188), so this is not a misreading. Independently, the tab keeps writing document content to disk after the user opted out, while watchForOfflineDisable (offline-erase.ts:172-216) erases the store on that same edge — so the still-mounted client re-creates entries the user asked to be deleted. I examined two refutation grounds and rejected both: the SDK's own apiKey/clientKey/docKey lock plus onLockRefused->giveUp only softens the second-tab case and leaves the freed election and post-opt-out writes untouched; and 'deliberate design' does not cover the inconsistency between the latched render branch and the non-latched lock release. Broken invariant plus post-opt-out disk writes on a path reachable by an ordinary Settings toggle is in-lane and blocking.

verdict.reason: Every element of the finding checks out in the repo. `dropAllForUser` records the loss marker with `this.evicted.add(docKey)` (wafflebase-doc-store.ts:858-862), and `evicted` is a per-instance `Set` (line 280) consulted only by `refuseIfEvicted` (617-626) on the `!header` branches of `appendChange` (540-541, 560-563) and `saveMeta` (597-603). No shared/static or cross-tab propagation of eviction state exists in the store (`isLive`, 306-311, only consults `this.touched` and the optional `isOpenElsewhere`). The erasing instance is never the SDK's: the live client writes through the store memoized in `DurableYorkieProvider` (durable-yorkie-provider.tsx:86-97, passed as `store` at 118), while the toggle-off erase runs on OfflineRuntime's own store (offline-runtime.tsx:55-70 → offline-erase.ts:205,30) and the logout erase on a throwaway store with no `isOpenElsewhere` (offline-erase.ts:123), where `isLive` is always false so nothing is even marked. Consequently a post-erase `appendChange` on the live store resolves as a silent no-op while `useDocumentDurability()` still answers true (durable-document-context.ts:67-69; `durable` only cleared via the SDK loss latch, durable-yorkie-provider.tsx:104-108,149-167), and the next `saveSnapshot` (489-508) re-creates the just-erased entry. The only candidate refutation — the feature is gated by `supportsClientKey()` (yorkie-capabilities.ts:76-82, collab-document-provider.tsx:196) — is a dependency-pin gate, not a guard that corrects this logic, so it does not refute.

finding.summary: `documentIdsIn` filters on `document.workspaceId` using what the call site passes as the workspace *slug*, so the workspace-delete purge silently matches nothing
finding.evidence: `deleteWorkspace(id)` is called as `deleteWorkspace(workspaceId!)` from the `/w/:workspaceId/settings` route param (workspace-settings.tsx:182), and that param is a slug — the same file navigates with `/w/${updated.slug}/settings` (line 103) and `/w/${remaining[0].slug}` (line 189). `documentIdsIn` then compares that slug to `document.workspaceId` (workspaces.ts:98), which is the document's workspace **id** (types/documents.ts:41, populated from the backend's `workspaceId` column). The filter therefore yields `[]` for every real deletion, `purgeOfflineDocuments([])` returns immediately (offline-erase.ts:148), and the local copies of a deleted workspace's documents stay on disk until the thirty-day sweep — exactly the outcome this code was added to prevent. The same mismatch applies to `removeMember`'s `documentIdsIn(workspaceId)` (line 138). Nothing fails loudly, so the no-op is invisible.

verdict.reason: Every premise checks out against the repository. `documentIdsIn` (workspaces.ts:94-103) filters `document.workspaceId === workspaceId`, and both callers pass a value that is a workspace slug in normal use: `deleteWorkspace(workspaceId!)` (workspace-settings.tsx:182) and `removeMember(workspaceId!, userId)` (workspace-settings.tsx:133) forward the raw `useParams()` route param from `/w/:workspaceId/settings` (App.tsx:147), and the app navigates to that route with slugs (Layout.tsx:65, home-or-redirect.tsx:26, workspace-settings.tsx:103 and 189). The compared field is the workspace UUID id: GET /documents returns Prisma rows spread verbatim (document.controller.ts:180-195 with attachMeta at 79-92), matching types/documents.ts:41. The backend accepting id-or-slug (workspace.service.ts:55-59, 225-233) is exactly why the slug flows through unnoticed. The filter therefore yields [] and purgeOfflineDocuments returns immediately on the empty-array check (offline-erase.ts:148), leaving local copies of a deleted workspace's documents on disk until the thirty-day sweep — the outcome the code exists to prevent — with no error surfaced (the catch at line 100 also returns [] silently). No guard, caller-side slug-to-id resolution, or normalization exists anywhere on these paths; the component even has workspace.id available but does not use it. The only case that accidentally works is the notification deep link using workspace.id (notification-text.ts:73), which does not protect the normal flow. Real, reachable in normal use, and major under the correctness rubric.

finding.summary: Nothing lowers `durable` when the store fails or refuses its writes, so the chip can promise `saved-locally` for work that is not on disk
finding.evidence: `SyncSignals.durable` is documented as the conjunction of three facts, one of which is 'the store is not failing its writes' (sync-status/sync-state.ts:40-48). The only thing that ever lowers it is `reportLoss`, latched solely from the SDK's `local-changes-dropped` event (durable-yorkie-provider.tsx:104-105, 160-163). A store write that rejects — `withQuotaRetry` giving up after one eviction (wafflebase-doc-store.ts:1081-1084), `refuseIfEvicted` throwing, or `open()` rejecting because IndexedDB is unavailable — never reaches `reportLoss`, and neither does the silent `!header` no-op path. `useDocumentDurability()` therefore keeps answering true and `deriveSyncState` keeps returning `saved-locally`, i.e. the chip tells the user their unsent work survives a reload when it is not on disk. This is the one direction the design says the feature must not fail in.
searchedFor: read wafflebase-doc-store.ts error paths (withQuotaRetry, refuseIfEvicted, appendChange, saveMeta)

verdict.reason: The absence claim holds. `durable` is published from exactly one production site (durable-yorkie-provider.tsx:106-109,121) as `!lost`, and `lost` is raised only by `reportLoss` (:105), whose sole caller is the `local-changes-dropped` subscription (:160-163). No store-failure signal can reach it: WafflebaseDocStoreOptions (wafflebase-doc-store.ts:104-138) exposes no error/notify callback, `withQuotaRetry` merely rethrows after one failed eviction (:1078-1084), and `refuseIfEvicted` throws a DOMException (:617-626) nothing in the app observes. So `useDocumentDurability()` (durable-document-context.ts:67-69) keeps returning true and use-sync-status.ts:75,220 keeps feeding `durable: true` into deriveSyncState, which returns `saved-locally` (sync-state.ts:85) — contradicting the documented conjunction in sync-state.ts:40-48 and the design table in docs/design/offline-local-persistence.md:373-392 ("Quota exhausted after eviction → false", "Store writes failing → false"). The repo's own task file states it outright: "Store *write* failures still do not lower it ... recorded as a known limitation" (docs/tasks/active/20260917-offline-wiring-todo.md:129-134). I found no counterexample anywhere: all other DurableDocumentScope uses are tests. Impact is a chip promising work survives a reload when it is not on disk — the direction the design says must never fail. Reachability is presently gated by supportsClientKey() at pin 0.7.22 (yorkie-capabilities.ts:24; package.json:66), which lowers today's exposure but does not refute the defect, since the bump is the intended switch.
